LESSON: READING ALOUD

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Reading
Topic 2.2: Reading aloud
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading aloud, part of Reading in Grade 4 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to introduce yourself to others? 2. How are Arabic alphabets different from those in other languages?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work jointly to articulate the symbols/characters of the Arabic alphabet,

2. articulate sounds using blend and digraphs in groups e.g saa..., qaa.

3. read Arabic syllables from a given display in groups,

4. take turns to read simple sentences on greetings and self- introduction,

5. create a letter bank of the Arabic alphabet and organise in a class portfolio. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work jointly to articulate the symbols/characters of the Arabic alphabet,
2. articulate sounds using blend and digraphs in groups e.g saa..., qaa.
3. read Arabic syllables from a given display in groups,
4. take turns to read simple sentences on greetings and self- introduction,
5. create a letter bank of the Arabic alphabet and organise in a class portfolio. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading aloud together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: This is developed as the learner builds on their organisation skills when creating a letter bank of the Arabic

alphabet and organises in a class portfolio.

• Communication and collaboration: This is developed as the learner enhances their speaking skills by articulating sounds

using blend and digraphs in groups e.g. saa..., qaa.

22

Values:
Responsibility: This is promoted as the learner engages in assigned duties when taking turns to read sentences on greetings and

self-introduction.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship: This is promoted as learners accommodate each other’s contributions and show kindness to each other as they work

in groups.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner is able to relate this concept on greetings and introduction as taught in all other languages.
